The Alamar Solution
## Enabling Precision Proteomics
By combining revolutionary sensitivity with robust multiplexing and automation, we’re not just improving existing methods — we’re enabling answers to entirely new categories of scientific questions and clinical applications.
## The NULISATM platform

### Ep.5: Oxford's Prof. John Todd on the Revolution Powering Precision Medicine
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why enabling technologies — from PCR to today's proteomics platforms — drive scientific discovery, and why Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay (including its Argo platform and CNS panel) has become central to his lab's work in type 1 diabetes, neuroinflammation, and biomarker-driven medicine.
![Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Episode4-prof.john_.png)
### Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why his lab at the Centre for Human Genetics added Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay and Argo platform to its proteomics toolkit — and what it revealed about interleukin-2 (IL-2) therapy in type 1 diabetes.
![Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_3.jpg)
### Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke
In this third episode of The Biomarker Edge, Dr. Cheryl Wellington from the University of British Columbia, discusses her work advancing fluid biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease, traumatic brain injury, and stroke. She shares insights on launching a new biomarker core facility, building collaborations with over 120 clinical partners, and expanding biomarker applications from pediatric to geriatric care. Dr. Wellington highlights how ultra-sensitive, multiplexed technologies like ARGO™ and NULISA™ are enabling low-volume specimen analysis, broad biomarker panels, and translational research that bridges clinical and pre-clinical models.
![Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_2.jpg)
### Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease
In this episode of The Biomarker Edge series, Dr. Nicholas Ashton from Banner Health explores the clinical utility of emerging plasma biomarkers—including p-tau217, NfL, GFAP, and others—in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. He discusses how high-sensitivity, multiplex platforms like NULISA™ are enabling researchers to detect low-abundance CNS proteins in blood with greater precision than ever before.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
